test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: An article's cost price is ₹300, and the marked price is mentioned as ₹1,032. What is the profit percentage of the seller if he sells it by allowing a discount of 50% on the marked price?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Cost Price (CP)** to **Selling Price (SP)** can be found directly.

MP = ₹1,032 and Discount = 50%.

SP = 50% of MP = 1,032 ÷ 2 = ₹516.

Profit = SP − CP = 516 − 300 = ₹216.

Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (216 ÷ 300) × 100 = 72%.

**∴ The correct answer is 72%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** CP = ₹300, MP = ₹1,032, Discount% = 50%
**Formulas:** SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 | Profit% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bd78aa8fce3f7aed85bf9a9f5223d21b56f62dcf067503639c7c9b479bb087bf.png] 

⇒ First, calculate **Selling Price (SP)** = 1,032 × (100 − 50) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 1,032 × 50 ÷ 100 = 516

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 516 − 300 = 216

⇒ Profit Percentage = (216 ÷ 300) × 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = 72%

**∴ The correct answer is 72%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

The **Marked Price (MP)** is the price printed on the label. Discount is always calculated on the MP to reach the Selling Price: SP = MP − Discount.

Profit/Loss on Cost Price

Unless otherwise stated, **Profit** or **Loss percentage** is always calculated based on the **Cost Price (CP)**.
